phone.comment: The SINGLE-PANE layout: under it a screen shows one pane at a time, a detail replacing its list with a way back, rather than the two side by side. 640 is the two-pane Inbox's list drawn twice, 2 x 320px: under it (where the sheet is already full-bleed) a detail beside a 320px list would be narrower than the list itself. Switch with (width < 640px), strictly under, as at breakpoint.shell.

md.comment: Tablets. The primary layout switch between stacked and multi-column.

shell.comment: Where the application shell stops being a rail beside a sheet and the rail becomes a drawer. DERIVED, at density 1: size.shell.rail 236px + size.shell.inset 8px + a 780px floor for the sheet = 1024px. The floor is the two-pane Inbox, a 320px list beside a 460px detail: the sheet the design needs to draw a list and its detail side by side. Switch with (width < 1024px), STRICTLY UNDER: at exactly 1024px the sheet is exactly its floor and the wide layout fits, so (max-width: 1024px) would draw the drawer at the one width the arithmetic says the rail still fits beside the sheet. It shares its number with lg by arithmetic, not by name: a change to the rail or the inset moves this step and leaves lg where it is. A media query cannot read a custom property, so a stylesheet that switches here spells the number, and @crewlethq/tokens/css/breakpoint is the generated partial that says what the number is.

2xl.comment: Large desktop, such as wide marketing hero containers.
